detail.body:
## Overview

Makes the AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill backend added in #57560 the default under `--gdn-prefill-backend auto` on ROCm gfx942 and gfx950, as discussed in that PR's review. It applies only to BF16 models with 128-dim linear-attention heads, and only when AITER is enabled and the build ships the FlyDSL kernels.

## Claims

* Lower time to first token by default on MI300X and MI355X for GDN models: −2.7% geomean on Qwen3-Next-80B (MI300X), −3.6% on Qwen3.8-2.4T (MI355X), about −1% to −2% on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (both). Decode throughput is unchanged.
* No accuracy change: GSM8K is identical on Qwen3-Next, and GSM8K and GPQA-Diamond were within noise in #57560.
* Fails safe. Any model, dtype, architecture or AITER build that FlyDSL cannot serve stays on Triton/FLA under `auto`, without a warning. An explicit `aiter_flydsl` request raises if the kernels are missing and otherwise warns before falling back to Triton/FLA, and `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` opts out.

## Validation

### Unit tests

```text
30 passed      # MI300X (gfx942), VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1, both files, no skips
ruff format --check: passed
ruff check: passed
```

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_rocm_layout_dispatch.py
```

* `test_auto_defaults_to_flydsl_on_gfx942_and_gfx950` checks the new default and each of its gates. `auto` selects FlyDSL on gfx942 and on gfx950, and stays on Triton when the architecture is gfx90a, the kernels are missing, `head_k_dim` is 64, or the dtype is FP16.
* `test_explicit_triton_opts_out_of_flydsl_default` checks that `triton` still selects Triton on an architecture where `auto` would pick FlyDSL.
* `test_kda_style_model_cannot_select_flydsl` is now parametrized over `aiter_flydsl` and `auto`, so the Kimi K3 exclusion also holds under the default.

### Serving and accuracy, gfx942: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct, TP2, MI300X (this branch)

`Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct` at revision `9c7f2fbe`, image `nightly-43b4aaea3e`, `--max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 256 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, one repeat per arm. The candidate runs with no backend flag, so it exercises `auto`; the control runs with `--gdn-prefill-backend triton`. Server logs confirm the kernel each arm used: `Using AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill kernel (requested=auto, head_k_dim=128)` for the candidate and `Using Triton/FLA GDN prefill kernel (requested=triton, ...)` for the control.

| ISL / OSL | Conc | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | Mean TPOT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8k / 1024 | 4 | 193.4 → 193.2 (−0.1%) | 617 → 601 ms (−2.5%) | 562 → 540 ms (−3.8%) | 20.10 → 20.14 ms |
| 8k / 1024 | 16 | 609.5 → 611.8 (+0.4%) | 1,717 → 1,658 ms (−3.4%) | 1,630 → 1,593 ms (−2.3%) | 24.58 → 24.54 ms |
| 8k / 1024 | 64 | 1,357.5 → 1,373.3 (+1.2%) | 5,371 → 5,239 ms (−2.5%) | 2,351 → 2,294 ms (−2.4%) | 41.75 → 41.34 ms |
| 60k / 600 | 4 | 32.6 → 32.8 (+0.5%) | 6,987 → 6,819 ms (−2.4%) | 5,945 → 5,806 ms (−2.3%) | 110.89 → 110.58 ms |

**Mean TTFT is lower at every point (geomean −2.7%).** Decode is flat, which is expected for a prefill-only change.

GSM8K, 5-shot, all 1,319 questions: flexible-extract 0.9606 → 0.9606, with 8 fixed and 8 broken (exact McNemar p = 1.00). Strict-match went from 0.7824 to 0.7923.

### Evidence carried over from #57560

The kernels and the gate are unchanged from #57560; only the default moves. The opt-in results there cover the remaining architecture and model combinations:

| Hardware | Model | TTFT, FlyDSL vs Triton | Accuracy, Triton → FlyDSL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MI355X (gfx950), TP8 | `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` | median geomean −3.6% over 16 cells, ISL 8k–128k, c 1–8 | GPQA-Diamond 0.9192 → 0.9343; GSM8K 0.9787 → 0.9825 |
| MI355X (gfx950), TP2 | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next | mean −0.5% to −1.4% in 11 of 12 cells, two passes each; +1.0% at 60k c=8 | — |
| MI300X (gfx942), TP2 | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` | mean −0.9% to −4.2%, geomean −1.9% over 4 cells | GSM8K 0.9697 → 0.9712 |

## Details

The change is one branch in `_resolve_gdn_prefill_backend`. When the user requests `auto` on ROCm, it returns `aiter_flydsl` under the same conditions an explicit request already has to meet, plus a gfx942/gfx950 check. Those conditions are BF16 activations, `head_k_dim == head_v_dim == 128`, and `rocm_aiter_ops.is_gdn_flydsl_prefill_available()`, which also honors `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER`.

* **Silent fallback under `auto`.** An explicit `aiter_flydsl` request raises when the kernels are missing and warns when the model is outside the gate, so a run never reports FlyDSL while running Triton. Under `auto` the user asked for nothing in particular, so a model outside the gate simply keeps today's backend.
* **Architecture allowlist.** FlyDSL has been validated only on gfx942 and gfx950, so other ROCm architectures such as gfx90a keep Triton/FLA.
* **Affected models.** In-tree, the gate admits the Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.8 GDN layers. 
* **Test pin.** `tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_rocm_layout_dispatch.py` now pins `gdn_prefill_backend=triton`. It checks the Triton path's numerics and output layout, and `auto` would otherwise route it to FlyDSL on gfx942/gfx950.
* **Limitation.** The size of the gain depends on the model: about −1% TTFT on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next against −3.6% on Qwen3.8-2.4T. Further FlyDSL kernel work is in progress in ROCm/aiter#5732.

Co-authored-by: Cursor

A unit test pins both messages.

WDYT? If you would rather have the runtime fallback, I think it could be a follow-up PR.
